newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian president backs female empowerment.
newsitem.headline: Indian president backs female empowerment.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma on Friday urged a 77-nation conference on women's empowerment to work towards rooting out social prejudices against women that have blocked their political progress.

"Politics as we know it today is very much a male bastion," Sharma told the meeting, where Namibian President Sam Nujoma and Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will join 250 lawmakers in working out strategies to bridge the gender gap.
"Though there is universal adult franchise (in India) and all women have the right to vote...their representation in legislatures is grossly inadequate."
Less than eight percent of India's lawmakers are women, who form nearly half the country's population of 930 million.

"It is only by empowering women through education and training, enabling them to achieve financial security, and ensuring their participation in decision-making processes that they can come into the mainstream," Sharma said.
"We must root out the prejudice against women and the negative attitude towards their participation in politics."

Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and former Iceland president Vigdis Finnbogadottir are also scheduled to speak at the five-day meeting organised by the Geneva-based Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU).
The IPU has described it as a follow-up to the United Nations Conference on Women held in Beijing in 1995.

India last year introduced a bill in its federal parliament to reserve one-third of all legislature seats for women, but its passage has been held up by technical wrangles on regional and caste considerations.
Critics say male lawmakers are using these grounds to prevent the bill from becoming law.
